body:
@lifeiscontent Currently I have mixed feelings about this example, the cookie is not `httpOnly`, `secure` (in production) or `sameSite`, which makes it hard to recommend this example.

I know that the current cookie auth example is like that, and that has to be fixed too before adding another not so secure auth example.
author: lfades

body: @lfades that's fine, I don't mind updating it. This was only my first pass at the work to get it released :)
author: lifeiscontent
lifeiscontent

body:
@lifeiscontent thank you for your time and effort. 

I am adding @rkotze (he's maybe unfamiliar with next.js) that might have an interesting input. He wrote a great article about JWT and httpOnly cookies for Apollo here: https://github.com/rkotze/rkotze.github.io/blob/master/_posts/2019-12-02-jwt-secure-apollo-client-graphql.md

My guess is that you should use `next-cookie` to set the cookies, by maybe updating the `res` you send inside the `WithApollo.getInitialProps`

```js
ctx.cookie.set('accessToken', token, {
    path,
    httpOnly: true,
    sameSite: 'Strict',  
    maxAge
})
```

In that case the `HttpLink` credentials should also be set to `"include"` I think. 

I might be very wrong about everything I just wrote. I will come back after a more indepth testing.
author: raduchiriac

body: @raduchiriac great, yeah, I'm not 100% on the protocols for security here either I figured I just put this POC up and have smarter people than me comment on it and then I'll do the work to make it better 👍
author: lifeiscontent

body: @raduchiriac  imao, the auth exemple should just be update with the change needed for an httpOnly Cookie use. As it's different then cookie with Next.
author: ppot

body:
@lifeiscontent Do this:

- Use `httpOnly` always.
- Set `secure` to `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'`.
- Use `sameSite`.
- Remove `next-cookies`. The cookie would be server-only (because of `httpOnly`), `res.setHeader` and [cookie](https://www.npmjs.com/package/cookie) should be enough

It would not be a state of the class auth method, but it's definitely better.

body: That sounds like a bug in the particular package (wrong publish). Also note that next does not compile node_modules, meaning you’re customizing webpack config to achieve that. Changing this will make resolving in typescript projects slower.
author: timneutkens

body:
@timneutkens every other framework (gatsby/create-react-app) resolves node_modules via JS not TS.

this might not be the right fix, but it definitely feels like a bug somewhere in the pipeline.

Within the typescript ecosystem its pretty common to compile your JS files along side your TS.

just because you haven't happened to use a node_module which does this doesn't make it not valid.

once its a node_module, (after compilation/published) it would seem pretty weird to consume TS. (which is currently happening)
author: lifeiscontent

body: @timneutkens also for the record, this wouldn't be an issue (for me) if styled-jsx worked in typescript alone, but since it doesn't I have to use babel to run the babel transforms to get the UI Kit I'm building to work correctly in different projects.
author: lifeiscontent

body:
Did a bunch more investigation into this and it seems that the TS compiler prefers `.js` files too so let's mirror that behavior, could you open a new PR and add tests for this behavior in `test/integration/typescript`.

I'll have to close this PR as it's fork has disappeared and I can't do a checkout for it.

body: I did some investigating on #9022 and this does not fix the case that is described in the initial issue as that one is related to how React is resolved. However I'd argue that the case described in the initial issue is a wrong project structure (deps not available) and that what you've fixed here is more important 👍
author: timneutkens

body:
I had the same error as #9022 when updating to ^9.06, as I've wrote in the comment https://github.com/zeit/next.js/issues/9022#issuecomment-570921527,  it is an issue of combination of 2 things, usage of sym-link & the fact that these libs had multiple instance in side server bundle...

I've tested, if one of the conditions is not apply, the bug is not reproduces.
When I've fixed the `next` regex, even sym-link started to work...
author: felixmosh

body: Could you add a test for this? Then we can ensure it keeps working.
author: timneutkens

body: Sure, @timneutkens can you suggest where to start? in which folder? how I can add an external dependency that has `*next/dist` in tests?
author: felixmosh

body:
I can confirm this PR does not fix #9022 in my case. See my https://github.com/zeit/next.js/issues/9022#issuecomment-571152664.

@timneutkens I wouldn’t say this is a result of a _wrong_ project structure, but rather an unusual project structure. However, I’m not the only one as can be seen in the original issue.
author: baldurh

body:
> I can confirm this PR does not fix #9022 in my case. See my [#9022 (comment)](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/issues/9022#issuecomment-571152664).
> 
> @timneutkens I wouldn’t say this is a result of a _wrong_ project structure, but rather an unusual project structure. However, I’m not the only one as can be seen in the original issue.

I've double checked, it solves the issue that I had.
I didn't had weird structure, but a mono-repo with usage of sym-link for building the production build & usage of `i18next` that got bundled in this case inside the server bundles.
author: felixmosh

body:
@felixmosh your case is fine and this PR will definitely fix it. Baldur's case is that there is no node_modules folder outside of the subdirectory and that causes React to not be resolved. Then an alias was added to next.config.js but that doesn't work as expected. Particularly what changed that caused that issue in particular is yarn PnP support.

Note that if you have a Node.js project and you would `require` the file it would break in exactly the same way, hence why I'm saying the project structure is wrong.
author: timneutkens

body: @timneutkens good point about Node.js. I guess you are right 😅

body:
@tim-phillips I'm watching #9022 because I've setup my project following the sample [NextJS with Firebase Hosting](https://github.com/firebase/functions-samples/tree/master/nextjs-with-firebase-hosting). As soon as I install React Bootstrap or React Material I get this error cause I end up with multiple react instances.

I would suggest to keep #9022 open or at least update the documentation with a better solution. It's a very common scenario libraries like the above to be used alongside React and the proposed Firebase file structure doesn't allow this at the moment.

body:
Also, if bundle size turns out to be a problem, I think we can probably also replace
```js
  if (path) {
    path = path.replace(/\/$/, '')
    // Append a trailing slash if this path does not have an extension
    if (!/\.[^/]+\/?$/.test(path)) path += `/`
  }
```
with
```js
  // Append a trailing slash if this path does not have an extension and does not have a trailing slash
  if (path && !/(\.[^/]+\/?$|\/$)/.test(path)) path += `/`
```
that should also shave off some of those bytes.

author: prateekbh

body:
Can't we just take a look at any of the other test runs on another branch? It looks like those tests are passing on other branches. Although I'm still trying to get myself up to speed on the integration suite and where all it runs so I could be misunderstanding what you're asking.

But just from a purely theoretical standpoint, this code will never make it to the else block which actually uses `PerformanceObserver`. So I think the behavior just needs to be adjusted. Perhaps by calling the method on the load event?
author: KB1RMA

body: @KB1RMA if the browser in tests has `PerformanceObserver` shouldn't it reach there?
author: prateekbh

body:
It does now that I've fixed the check for it existing on `window`. But I don't think it's behaving as it was designed. It almost looks like the observer is being registered too late in the lifecycle and the callback is never actually executed for paint metrics. At least from my brief amount of time debugging and reading docs on `PerformanceObserver`.

**Edit:** On second glance... is this else block even required at all? Shouldn't this just work fine calling `performance.getEntriesByType()` on the load event? And ditch the entire `PerformanceObserver` check and subsequent instantiation
author: KB1RMA

body:
I'm proposing pulling the `PerformanceObserver` out of this. I don't see how it could stream `first-paint` to the component this late in the lifecycle. It needs to be pulled retroactively from the performance api.

Unless there's a way to get fancy and stream it to local storage before hydration, then read it in later? But that seems pretty complex

body:
@thomaswang If this fixed the bug for you, then
1. Did you change anything else? Try putting back `"styled-components"` and see if it re-introduces the bug.
2. If you run `npx nls why babel-core` (to analyze your dependencies), do you see any Babel v6? There was an edge case in Babel 6 where `babel-plugin-styled-components` != `styled-components`.
3. Are you able to reproduce this bug by calling Babel directly? If so, please report it to https://github.com/babel/babel/issues
author: nicolo-ribaudo

body: Changed it back to `styled-components` and everything checks out, I'm also on Babel v7. Sorry about that! I think the error might've occurred from 2 different static builds?

"Access user data (token in this case) on the header or other Layout components its a real necessity." - That's true, but what you need is the data, not the token.

A custom `_app` will affect all pages in the app, you may not need auth info for all pages, therefore we don't recommend doing this, and specially if `_app` has `getInitialProps`, which will turn all pages into serverless functions.

@VictorAssis Thank you for taking the time of creating a PR. For the reasons above I'm going to close it.

The example should remove the token from the client code, so it would only be available for API calls, and won't be accessible through the client js. Meaning that the current example is not very secure, and this doesn't help.
author: lfades

body:
"That's true, but what you need is the data, not the token." - This is also true. I did not implement the login by saving other user data in cookies because I thought it might get too complex for the example, but I can change it here.

"A custom _app will affect all pages in the app, you may not need auth info for all pages, therefore we don't recommend doing this, and specially if _app has getInitialProps, which will turn all pages into serverless functions." - I understand that, but if a site has a user info in the header and use the layout in all pages, i think that dont exist way to avoid this. Im right?

Thinking of what you said, if I return the Layout component to the pages, use the HOC only in pages with Layout component and save other user data in token, do I solve these problems?

Sorry for insist @lfades , i'm having a great experience with Next Js and i want to contribute.
author: VictorAssis
lfades

body:
@lfades I'm having some questions on how to remove the token from client. When you refer to having the token on the server, do you mean api endpoints or getInitialProps?

I imagine these two scenarios:

**1. Access cookies only in api**

When the api receive a request in login endpoint, then she save the token in the cookies and return a flag of success to the client. The profile endpoint directly access the token to get the data.

The withAuth needs to consult the profile endpoint always (to get user info for header) or consult once and save the data in localstorage.

To logout its necessary to create another endpoint who clean the cookie from api.

The authorization header would not be necessary in this case.

**2. Api doesn't change**

Here I am having trouble figuring out a way to not access the token on the client.

Today, the login function in auth.js is responsible for saving the cookie and it runs on the client side. This is a problem?

If not, withAuth's getInitialProps will check if it is on the client or server side for API call data or directly from the cookie. In this way, will also save user information in the cookie.

And to logout, will we remove the cookie on the client (as it works today) or will we create an exit page that will remove cookies on the server?

Thanks for help!
author: VictorAssis

body: @VictorAssis You are right, API routes would be needed for login/logout, and only the API routes will have access to the cookie, which should never be sent to the client, you may want to read the converstaion here: https://github.com/zeit/next.js/pull/9913

body:
@aganglada Hi, thank you for the PR, can you describe what feature was enabled, what is RTL and why does it deserve its own example in the readme please 🙏 

For example, in the `amp` example:
```md
## The idea behind the example

This example shows how to create AMP pages using Next.js and the AMP feature. It shows a normal page (non-AMP), an AMP only page, and a hybrid AMP page.
```
author: lfades

body:
@lfades Thank you for the feedback, I added a description of the example. Let me know if you find it useful.

I think i's going to be useful to have the example. There is no really good documentation from the SC side (which I intent to improve as well) on this as they just released it. I think there is going to be many people asking how to implement this (I've followed the release all over and I've had the same issue).

body:
Looking forward to try this 👍

Is the idea to align `getServerProps` with the RFC regarding returning props under a specific `props`-key at a later stage, or has that idea been changed to more align with current `getInitialProps` usage?

One example for when it would be useful to return options beside props could be to determine if certain page data is allowed to be stale on page navigation, related to this:
> We can investigate caching for history navigations in follow-ups if we think it is desirable
https://github.com/zeit/next.js/pull/10077#discussion_r368068560

body:
@kmjennison thanks for answering my question about adapting `getServerSideProps` at https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/8672#issuecomment-633277961

After I tried your suggestion and switching to `getServerSideProps`, I get the error `Error: You can not use getInitialProps with getServerSideProps. Please remove getInitialProps.`. I guess that's because `_document` is using `getInitalProps` https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/34f82a996b42671950be9af94b5a9a8c00bf3413/examples/with-firebase-authentication/pages/_document.js#L35

However, I am planning to use both `getServerSideProps` and `getInitialProps` on different pages. Because some pages require fetching from my backend, the others will fetch from 3rd party directly (without going through my backend if running on client-side) meanwhile supporting SSR. 

Do you have experience supporting `getServerSideProps` meanwhile using Firebase Auth, and occasionally use `getServerSideProps` or `getInitialProps`?

body:
@timneutkens it looks like your two remaining failing tests are because you're attempting to use the plain CSS `@import` but Sass has its own `@import`. When the imported file is `.scss` and not `.css` it will run the Sass version not the native CSS version. https://sass-lang.com/documentation/at-rules/import#plain-css-imports

`@import` for Sass files is discouraged.

body:
> Can we please flag all of these changes behind a experimental flag?

@Timer I could add a flag that omits the `sass-loader` specific test blocks, but then the loaders for error warnings, `file-loader`, and such wouldn't be behind the flag because they're paired with CSS: `test: /\.(css|scss|sass)$/`

The only way I can think of to make a flag work simply is a duplicate file or `css()` function (a la `sass()`) separate from the original that contains the new implementation so the flag determines to fully use the current function or the new CSS + Sass function.

Would like to know your thoughts before attempting.

PR: https://github.com/zeit/next.js/pull/8980
author: jhiggins-thrillist

body: Hi, we changed back to `async` after investigation and recommendation from the Chrome team. We plan to re-introduce the experiment to switch between the two modes to enable more investigation
author: ijjk

body:
> It looks like this hotfix breaks this experimental feature that was introduced in v9.1.2
> 
> PR: #8980

We'll reintroduce this in the future, but do note, experimental features may change in breaking ways, be removed, or break your application in between patch releases.

the base repository is a `lerna` repo with:

```
components/*
sites/*
```

Where `next.js` apps reside under `sites`, and shared // reusable components sit under `components`.

This was the issue and fix I found elsewhere. I'll look into this further now that I have a test to experiment against but hopefully the tests will help us be sure it's working in whichever order.

For reference the error is:
```
Failed to compile.·

./styles/global.scss
Error: resolve-url-loader: CSS error
  file:///next.js/test/integration/scss-fixtures/loader-order/styles/global.scss:1:4: Unknown word

author: alejalapeno

body:
I've figured out the steps to create the error and produced an example repo here: https://github.com/alejalapeno/next-sass-loader-order

I replicated the example from `resolve-url-loader` docs (with file name changes to match Next's structure.)

Requirements:
- Applies only to global Sass. Does not affect modules.
- Sass file _must_ have Sass features. Seems to be skipped over by the `sass-loader` otherwise.
- Loader then fails on several features, including (crucially) not being able to resolve URL's. The fail on double-slash comments is just an easy way to test for the same issue.

The removal of the preprocessor reversal is the only thing I've found to solve it. Removal of the reversal still seems to resolve both module + global urls.

Interestingly enough, removal of the `reverse()` for modules loaders in `modules.ts` has the opposite effect and breaks them in the same manner...

author: ijjk

body:
This approach should handle both the process being killed/crashing or the `distDir` being cleared often as it users [proper-lockfile](https://npmjs.com/package/proper-lockfile) and it's lockfile method handles a stale lock even if it isn't able to remove it before the process exits:

> When a lock is successfully acquired, the lockfile's mtime (modified time) is periodically updated to prevent staleness. This allows to effectively check if a lock is stale by checking its mtime against a stale threshold

Here's an example of it handling SIGTERM and SIGKILL (sorry for low-res can't use MP4 on GitHub)
![Kapture 2020-01-24 at 9 54 04](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22380829/73082659-80c71e80-3e8f-11ea-8e27-5cb67c2100b2.gif)

body:
Hi @rwieruch, thank you so much for the PR!

I believe `next-env.d.ts` should just be limited to Next-specific typings, as the name suggests.

If you wanted to add additional types, I think it's better to create *separate* `d.ts` files that are named accordingly. For example, if you want to import `mdx` files, you should create a file called `mdx.d.ts` (this is suggested by [the official MDX doc](https://mdxjs.com/advanced/typescript)).

The question is where to add this file, but this `.d.ts` can be added **anywhere** in the project directory because Next.js’s tsconfig by default [includes all files ending in `.ts`](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/5bcd33fccbb771d8004a568b67e6e03b301c5764/packages/next/lib/verifyTypeScriptSetup.ts#L281) in the compile pipeline. So `mdx.d.ts` can be added to the top-level alongside `next-env.d.ts` or under `types` directory, for example - the location doesn't matter.

Of course, this is not clear in the documentation. What do you think about changing it like this?

---

A file named `next-env.d.ts` will be created in the root of your project. This file ensures Next.js types are picked up by the TypeScript compiler. **You cannot remove it**, and you shouldn’t need to edit it.

If you need to add custom type declarations, you can create a `[any-name].d.ts` file and place it anywhere in the project directory, and it will automatically be picked up by the compiler by default. For instance, if you’re using [next-mdx](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/packages/next-mdx) and want to import `mdx` files, create `mdx.d.ts` anywhere in the project directory and [follow this guide](https://mdxjs.com/advanced/typescript) from the MDX docs.

---

- I added the wording: "you shouldn’t need to edit it"
- I also used the wording "if you need to add custom type...." instead of "but doesn't offer TypeScript support" because packages might not offer TS support but the types might be on [DefinitelyTyped](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped). You'd only need to create a `d.ts` file if the types are not on DefinitelyTyped or if you're importing non-standard file types.
- I used the mdx example because it already has a documentation page with the code sample - so no need to include the code here.

Let me know what you think!

body:
Putting all declarations in `next-env.d.ts` does not scale well. In my projects, I keep declarations in paths like

```
declarations/package-name.d.ts
declarations/@scoped/package-name.d.ts
```

The compiler picks them well, the folder structure scales perfectly too 👍

body: I'll put out another request to take another look at this.  Are there any downsides of merging it? The benefits have been laid out well in the related issues by @bluelovers and others. You don't need to be convert next.config.js to benefit from this.  There is still no concise reference for next.config.js.  Having a NextConfig type and using it via JSDoc brings an always-current reference directly into the editor.

body: Would deducing the base URL from the incoming request be a viable option?
author: janus-reith

body: @janus-reith Not really, that may cause security issues in some hosting providers.
author: lfades
janus-reith

body:
> But is there any other way besides using the request or manually providing the url in env?
Also, one that is not specific to vercel deployments.

Not that I'm aware of. Adding `VERCEL_URL` is possible but for other platforms they'll have to provide a similar variable. It also highly depends on your setup as not everyone does immutable deploys.
author: timneutkens

body: Would you accept an example which uses `VERCEL_URL`, and maybe just throws an error indicating you need to provide something like `BASE_URL` if that is not present?
author: janus-reith

body:
@janus-reith Nope, we don't do a lock in with Vercel in any of our examples, unless absolutely necessary, the only exception I can think of right now is the multi zones example.

The best thing you can do is to try something similar to what's in the [api-routes-apollo-server-and-client](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/api-routes-apollo-server-and-client) example, for SSR it uses the resolvers directly (which is even better than making an API call), and the client makes API requests.
author: lfades

body:
@lfades While I appreciate that attitude regarding lock in, it seems like we're stuck with this then.

At the same time, somehow it seems disproportionate to me to not showcase having an easily manageable federated serverless apollo Gateway and I can definitely see usecases for this. Regarding the other apollo example you linked, what do you mean when you suggest trying somthing similar? I might be missing the point, but this doesn't cover spliting concerns across multiple routes, which makes sense for more complex APIs that involves some startup time or where parts might scale differently.
author: janus-reith

body: @janus-reith First, this is only an issue because the API lives in the same app, but also because of that, you can take advantage of the Schema Link (iirc) and use the resolvers directly only for SSR, what this means is that instead of making a request to your API, the Node.js build of the app will include the resolvers and execute them directly. startup time may be higher but that's nothing compared to the bandwidth used in an API call.
author: lfades

body:
@lfades But there is some data which I might prefer to fetch on the client side instead of having it baked into a page in the server side, I think it would be reasonable in many cases to still have the page static and only fetch dynamic (in my case, authenticated) data on the client side, instead of Server-Rendering that page each time?
My expectation here would be, that in the end serving static pages and in some cases, return data over api, takes less computing time than rendering the page on the server each time it is requested?

And besides just the data that is fetched, that API could also include some amount of Mutations, e.g. in an ecommerce application for checkout, editing a user profile, updating a product, and many more, and for these Mutations it would be reasonable to split them across multiple lambdas, depending on the complexity of the code they involve?

While I agree that in many cases it could make sense to just separate that api from the frontend altogether, I think this way gives an really easy entrypoint to just be able to use and deploy it in one go.
E.g. I actually have a specific usecase for this, where my API already is a separated Nodejs application, with its logic split into many separated modules - What I'm trying now is to get these modules to work inside Nextjs API routes as an alternative approach of using it, which might reduce friction in getting started with the project for people that might be uncomfortable with having to deploy multiple services, and also it would give the possibility to have easy deployments on vercel and hopefully other platforms, as I currently consider that entry barrier a bit too high for many people.
That apollo federation nextjs example here was helpful for me to confirm in the first place that this was a possibility the way I imagined it.
author: janus-reith

body:
> My expectation here would be, that in the end serving static pages and in some cases, return data over api, takes less computing time than rendering the page on the server each time it is requested?

Yes, always!

You can go for SSG for some data and then do client side data fetching, using something like SWR to fetch authenticated data in the client, without having to SSR the entire page, and in that case an absolute URL of the deployment is not needed as you could do relative requests in this case, e.g: `fetch('/api/user')`
author: lfades

body:
@lfades Thanks for confirming, yes that is basically what I'm doing.
Auth-related stuff is handled on the client, by fetching some api route which reads an encrypted cookie (using swr actually), and if successful, an auth header is added on the apollo client, which will then make further authenticated request to an  currently external API using GraphQL.

If I would build something from scratch and it would only be intended to be used with that nextjs frontend, I could just split concerns into API routes right away. Using all that logic I have now in one big graphql lambda instead seems really inefficient, and so I was happy to be able split things into multiple api routes.

What I was wondering now is if you would consider the API Route Federation approach bad in general? For that consideration, leaving out the queries which if possible should go a direct route and not be fetched, and only considering the various mutations. I'm not sure if I understood your position on that yet.
author: janus-reith

body: @janus-reith As long as it works and doesn't require an absolute URL

These tests are supposed to fail because the routes manifest file of the snapshot used in the tests is wrong

author: timneutkens

body:
> Unlikely this will be landed based on the described issue. We'll potentially support opting into React profiling similarly to Strict mode, but have to discuss that first.
> 
> (Replying early to prevent you from spending a lot of time on this).

The issue is more general than just the one described. Basically if you have *any* third party library, or your own code that relies on process.env.NODE_ENV being set to development.. for a development environment, then the current phases are insufficient if you want to test with a static build. 

If static builds matched non-static builds more closely this would be less of an issue.

body:
I actually have noticed some other things too. I won't open an issue or anything as we can just discuss here and I'd love to help.

It looks like than just the package.json stuff changed since this tutorial was written (nice improvements!).  Let me know if I can help, would love to re-write this if there is a need as I do a lot of technical blogging myself, and I am about to rebuild my Wordpress blog (https://sethreid.co.nz) in Next.js so could be a good candidate to update the tutorial. 

I still found the tutorial invaluable and easy to follow but here are some things I found:

- The tutorial says I will get a 404 when I go to http://localhost:3000 but in fact I got this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4713713/73969044-6c583c80-48f9-11ea-9f1c-92eca898952a.png)

- At least some of the rest of the step are already completed in my app after running `npm install next react react-dom`:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4713713/73970008-2f8d4500-48fb-11ea-8234-9e4bd2c485f1.png)

- The answers for the quizzes are pre-filled with the correct answer although I've never done the tutorial:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4713713/73970061-45026f00-48fb-11ea-9015-ee0e7c9293a1.png)

author: BiscuiTech

body:
@BiscuiTech Currently I am not a fan of adding more examples regarding apollo.
We already have a lot examples, that are hard to maintain. 

Maybe we can add a docs directory where we explain different strategies regarding those PRs.
Here are some topics we might want to cover in there.

- Drawbacks of using Apollo (e.g.: bundle size increase, performance)
- Apollo SSR
- Apollo partial SSR
- Apollo manual SSR
- Apollo SSG
- Apollo Server
- Apollo server side auth
    - Especially drawbacks of this approach (caching issues, performance & security)
- Apollo client side auth
- Apollo `_app.js` vs Apollo `<somePage>.js`

As soon as I have time I'll try to write down some of the thoughts I currently have in my head. 
Of course PRs are always welcome.

body:

body:
@Linux249 thanks for your feedback. I will try to look into the issue regarding errors in the future. A good reproduction example could help a lot.

I've also already looked into `@apollo/client@3.0.0-beta.36`. Currently I decided to wait for it to be stable. This is because:

- currently  `@apollo/client@3.0.0-beta.36` increased its bundle size compared to Version 2 (this is a nogo from my point of view since apollo-client is already way to big).
- `@apollo/client@3.0.0-beta.36` currently has a lot of bugs when it comes to ssr.
- Migrating from apollo-client to @apollo/client is not trivial, because of npm/yarn issues in the dependency tree. 

So lets wait for a stable release until we update this example.

body:
It seems that purgecss has a new required option: the css files to purge.
Although it is not clearly documented, the types show it as required: https://github.com/FullHuman/purgecss/blob/98bbd5ca6d553e00af913acaf04ce8b9ed6f0df3/packages/postcss-purgecss/src/types/index.ts#L16

That is what @mekeor wants to improve in this example, I think.

body: I always put css paths in the `content` property and it still works as expected

Thanks for the PR!

Thanks!

body:
@ijjk have you heard of [`envalid`](https://github.com/af/envalid)? Curious if we could use it here or at least get inspired by. 

---

In some of my Next.js projects I have a file called `env.config.js`, which exports an object with cleaned env variables (result of passing through envalid). When I use those values in `next.config.js`, I'm not just sure that all my vars are of the right type, but are also of the acceptable value range etc. (common examples are host or port). This is thanks to a rich variety of [bult-in validators](https://github.com/af/envalid#validator-types) plus the ability to write [custom ones](https://github.com/af/envalid#custom-validators).

If any of my expected env vars is missing or is wrong, there'll be an early exit in `env.config.js` with a useful message, explaining what I've messed up. What is cool about this approach is that I even get typescript code intellisense and checks if I have [`--checkJs`](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/type-checking-javascript-files.html) in `tsconfig.json` 👀
author: kachkaev

body: The config has to be a json file as it'll integrate into tooling hence why it has to be of a certain format and we don't want to introduce extra dependencies (only dotenv).
author: timneutkens

body: IC. Is the JSON schema you are using somewhat established or specific to Next.js?
author: kachkaev

body: @kachkaev it ties into Next.js, there's no established solution for this problem as far as I've researched (besides `.env` but that only covers the loading of environment variables)
author: timneutkens

body: Just curious, which tooling are you planning to integrate your solution into? If it supports JS, `envalid` seems to fit too. The problem with JSON it only supports declarative constraints, which makes it hard to check for peculiar things. Of course one can come up with fields with number ranges, regexps (hosts, emails), but there's always a limit and the further the limit, the harder to write declarations. It's hard to beat the ability to call functions for validation, which explains why tools like prettier and eslint support JS in their config files. Perhaps, relying on envalid (or at least allowing JS in validators) is not such a bad thing 🤔
author: kachkaev

body:
> Just curious, which tooling are you planning to integrate your solution into

The Next.js CLI, hosting solutions like Now etc.


I don't really see how you'd want to check for "valid email" etc in environment variables tbh. Overall you'd just want to have a required/not required.
author: timneutkens

body:
> I don't really see how you'd want to check for "valid email" 

That's how it's done with [`envalid`](https://github.com/af/envalid) (in, say, `env.config.json`):

```js
const envalid = require('envalid')

const env = envalid.cleanEnv(process.env, {
    API_KEY:           envalid.str(),
    ADMIN_EMAIL:       envalid.email({ default: 'admin@example.com' }),
    SOME_BOOLEAN_FLAG: envalid.bool({ desc: 'My boolean flag' })
})

module.exports = env
```

Then in `next.config.json`:

```js
const env = require('./env.config.js');
console.log(env.ADMIN_EMAIL); // never logs an invalid email
console.log(env.SOME_BOOLEAN_FLAG); // always logs a proper boolean, not a string
```

If you want external tools to access validation rules, they can either run `env.config.js` and monitor if it tries an early exit. Alternatively, `env.config.js` could export just the second argument of `envalid.cleanEnv(..., ...)`:

```js
const envalid = require('envalid')

module.exports = {
    API_KEY:           envalid.str(),
    ADMIN_EMAIL:       envalid.email({ default: 'admin@example.com' }),
    SOME_BOOLEAN_FLAG: envalid.bool({ desc: 'My boolean flag' })
}
```

body:
@lfades thanks for this PR - great to see how someone leverages/interprets passport in this lambda world.

We have fought this alert on a number of endpoints in the pages/api directory and have seen conflicting reports on whether the alert is legit or benign. So I figured I'd ask you about the alert in the next logs and see if you could provide any color for this example and maybe the team could also provide any color on whether this alert is going to continue to show and how it should be interpreted/handled. Btw, happy to create a separate ticket if it's easier to track.

Steps to Reproduce.
```
1. npm run dev (in examples/with-passport)
2. navigate to '/login'
3. Login with any credentials
4. See log below
```

```
API resolved without sending a response for /api/login, this may result in stalled requests.
```
author: followbl

body:
@followbl That's a false positive, downside of having an API endpoint with `express`, but it's also the only way of using Passport. You can see in the network tab that the endpoint finishes with `200` and with the body sent by the endpoint.

@Timer Can we do something here about this?

body: If it's asked under `create-next-app --example` it's unlikely anyone will use it as it's not easy to know it exists. I'm not opposed to asking it as part of the normal flow, but it should have an option to not do so.
author: timneutkens

body: @timneutkens  "I'm not opposed to asking it as part of the normal flow": Should we keep it as an additional step as introduced initially in this PR?
author: lfades

body:
> @timneutkens "I'm not opposed to asking it as part of the normal flow": Should we keep it as an additional step as introduced initially in this PR?

Yeah there's basically 2 options:
- Add it as part of the default flow unless `--example <something>` is provided explicitly
- Don't add this feature

Hiding it under `--example` will cause it to not be used by users, so then it's not worth the additional install weight

body:
> @aralroca
> For me it was simply:
> 
> `next.config.js`:
> 
> ```diff
> - const withSass = require("@zeit/next-sass")
> - module.exports = withSass({
> +module.exports = {
>  /*Your config here*/
> - })
> + }
> ```

@balazsorban44  However, if you have sass without "css modules" into the component level, is not so trivial, isn't it?
author: aralroca

body: True, sorry!
author: balazsorban44

body:
```
find . -depth -name "*.scss" -exec sh -c 'mv "$1" "${1%.scss}.module.scss"' _ {} \;
```

Then search/replace in the codebase: `.scss` -> `.module.scss`

author: yuyichao

body: Why not use the file path and URL builders that are standard?
author: ethanwillis

body:
@yuyichao A path containing a double trailing slash can never be a subpath of the resolved/absolute requested path. In that case, `isServeable` will always return false.

@ethanwillis Are you referring to the logic of `isServeable` or this particular fix? In the latter case, I think the fix is quite straightforward and does not introduce new dependencies. Moreover, to which file path and URL builders do you refer exactly?
author: fabianishere

body: Ah, thx. I didn’t realized that you are searching for this prefix. The need to do this sounds a little strange but at least the local behavior you are descending makes sense.....
